question: Which statement best describes Incremental migration with allowJs?
options: any is a legitimate temporary tool while migrating, but it must be contained: prefer unknown where you can, isolate any to file/module boundaries, and mark debts with // TODO or a custom type alias (type TODO = any) you can grep and remove later. Never let any silently spread through inference.

allowJs lets TypeScript compile and type-aware-check .js files alongside .ts, so you can introduce TypeScript without converting everything at once. Pair it with checkJs (or per-file // @ts-check) to start surfacing type errors in existing JS. This keeps the app building the entire time.

Convert file-by-file, usually starting at the leaves of the dependency graph (utilities with few dependencies) and working up. Renaming .js to .ts turns on full checking for that file; fix its errors, then move to the next. Avoid a big-bang rename — it produces an unreviewable error avalanche.

Don't enable strict: true on day one. Turn on individual flags progressively — start with noImplicitAny off, get the project compiling, then enable noImplicitAny, then strictNullChecks, etc., fixing fallout at each step. Each flag is a separate, reviewable migration milestone.
